subject: Post-demo: Dedicated capacity fine-grain sizing & GPU tradeoffs
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:13:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + short list of sizing clarifications (Dedicated)

Hi Sophie — thanks again for joining the demo this morning. Quick recap and the specific items we need to finalize to give you a firm Dedicated capacity recommendation. I’ve summarized our call notes at the top and listed the clarifying asks below.

Call notes (short):
- ClearCart will run product search + conversational assistant for shoppers across web and mobile.
- Typical request = 80–200 tokens output, prompt ~120 tokens; sometimes longer when returning attribute lists.
- Peak concurrent sessions today ~220; expected growth to ~1k over 12 months with marketing season spikes.
- Latency SLO target: p95 generation < 250ms for 95% of catalog queries; up to 500ms OK for complex assistant flows.
- Primary concern: predictable latency and cost containment. Data residency: US-only.

Clarifying asks (please reply inline or attach traffic profile):
1) Can you confirm expected average tokens per-generation and average prompt tokens for the two primary workflows (search vs assistant)?
2) Expected steady-state TPS (requests per second) and peak TPS during campaign spikes (15–30 minute window). If you use batching on your side, note that too.
3) Any on-device session affinity or KV cache expectations? Do you expect long context reuse (e.g., multi-turn cart conversations with >1k token KV caches)?
4) Any hard requirements for on-prem/VPC vs Dedicated? From our talk it sounded like Dedicated (reserved pool in US) is your preferred path unless compliance needs push you to a VPC. Confirm please.

What we’ll deliver after we get these answers: a short, line-item SKU recommendation (GPU family, #GPUs in reserved pool, concurrency per-GPU target), expected p95 latency and cost per 1M tokens, and a pilot plan for a 2-week reserved pool test.

Attachments: I’ve attached an initial SKU options PDF with how we map workloads to A100/H100/L4 families and a lightweight sizing worksheet.

Next steps: Sophie to send traffic CSV and token profiles; we’ll follow up with a recommended SKU by EOD next Wednesday (May 30).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + short list of sizing clarifications (Dedicated)

Thanks Vanessa — attaching the traffic profile and a short answers file. Answers inline below.

Inline answers:
1) Tokens: Search flow (single-turn) = prompt ~80 tokens, response ~60 tokens average. Assistant flow (multi-turn) = prompt ~180 tokens, response ~240 tokens average. We do hold ~800–1,200 token context for cart assistants in ~5% of sessions.
2) TPS: steady-state ~7–10 TPS (across web + mobile). Peak during campaigns: bursts up to ~85 TPS sustained for ~20 minutes; single-minute spikes up to ~130 TPS.
3) Session affinity: yes — we try to keep affinity to reduce cold KV misses. Expect to reuse KV caches for multi-turn flows; typical KV cache size 800–1,200 tokens for those sessions.
4) Deployment mode: prefer Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) for now; VPC/on-prem only if legal asks change.

We also noted that we want predictable per-call cost and a clear rollback if latency jumps during spikes.

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + short list of sizing clarifications (Dedicated)

Sophie — great data, thanks. Based on the profile you sent, here’s a concise recommended Dedicated SKU and operational notes. I’ll keep this high level; Ben and Karthik will propose exact reserved counts and the pilot schedule.

High-level recommendation (Quick read):
- GPU family: H100 (FP16 / quantized int8-friendly) for production pool. Rationale: your peak burst spikes and multi-turn KV cache requirements benefit from higher single-GPU throughput and memory headroom. H100s provide best headroom for >1k token KV reuse and keep p95 below 250ms with conservative batching.
- Reserved pool sizing (pilot): start with 4 H100s as a reserved pool for a 2-week pilot (autoscale burst + buffer to keep headroom during 20-min spikes). If pilot metrics meet p95 targets, move to 8 H100s reserve for production headroom scale.
- Concurrency per-GPU target: configure 6–10 concurrent requests per GPU for low-latency path (depends on model). For heavy assistant flows where KV is large, we’ll reduce concurrency through affinity pins.
- TPS handling: expected steady-state (7–10 TPS) easily covered. For 130 TPS spikes, batching + short-term burst capacity is required. With 4 H100s we estimate queueing risk for sustained 85 TPS; that’s why pilot includes autoscale burst to 2 additional H100s on demand.
- Token mix & batching: set automatic batching window 5–10ms for web search flows (short outputs), allow larger batching for assistant flows when latency budget allows. Enable prefix KV caching for session affinity.
- Quantization: recommend int8 quantized model variants for search flows (cost savings) and FP16 for assistant flows where quality sensitivity is higher. We’ll ship mixed-precision profiles so routing can choose variant by route.

Operational asks for PO / pilot:
- Confirm we can run pilot on US-resident Dedicated pool and that ClearCart will provide a test key and anonymized sample logs for regression checks.
- Approve pilot budget for 2-week reserved pool (we’ll include burst credits in the quote).

Deliverables next:
1) Ben will send a line-item quote with pilot pricing and expected cost per 1M tokens.
2) Karthik will schedule a technical deep-dive to lock concurrency knobs and model variant mapping (30–45 mins).
3) I will create a pilot checklist and SLA floor to validate p95 latency and fallback behaviors.

Attachments: I’m attaching the sizing worksheet (filled with our preliminary mapping) and a short FAQ for Dedicated pilots.

Thanks — talk soon.
Vanessa Ortiz
